subject.title: iOS remote pairing UX: QR crash, onboarding paste fails, Settings paste works (cellular); feedback on edge auth + mobile wss://

question: Should OpenClaw document public `wss://` mobile pairing as an advanced supported recipe, and if so should the supported shape require a separate mobile hostname without HTTP SSO plus OpenClaw token/device bootstrap?
rationale: The reporter proved the pattern can work, but blessing it changes public exposure and trusted-proxy guidance, so the final docs need maintainer security/product intent.

options.title: Document advanced public wss recipe
options.body: Add docs that recommend Tailscale Serve by default and separately cover split admin/mobile hostnames, no browser SSO on mobile pairing, token/device bootstrap, `trustedProxies`, Settings paste, and release caveats.

options.title: Tailscale-only recommendation
options.body: Keep custom public tunnels as unsupported advanced operator territory and document only Tailscale Serve for remote mobile pairing.

options.title: Design edge-auth support first
options.body: Keep this open as a design item for service-token or app-embedded edge auth before documenting public `wss://` as supported.

recommendation.title: Document advanced public wss recipe
recommendation.body: Add docs that recommend Tailscale Serve by default and separately cover split admin/mobile hostnames, no browser SSO on mobile pairing, token/device bootstrap, `trustedProxies`, Settings paste, and release caveats.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the adjacent route-list fix and merged the QR scanner fix, and the remaining decision sits across pairing, auth, docs, and release posture.
